fixes_applied: Replaced Steel01 with Hardening material (exact bilinear kinematic hardening, Hkin=b*E/(1-b)) for story 1
Replaced Steel01(b=1e-8) with ElasticPP (exact elastic-perfectly plastic) for stories 2-4

ROOT CAUSE FIX: Stiffness-proportional Rayleigh damping (ops.rayleigh alpha,0,beta,0) does not function in this OpenSeesPy version (ops312). Fixed by implementing stiffness-proportional damping via explicit uniaxialMaterial Viscous dampers in parallel with each spring element.
Changed *DYNAMIC ALPHA from -0.05 to 0.0 (pure Newmark beta=0.25, gamma=0.5 instead of HHT)
Changed ISOTROPIC hardening to KINEMATIC hardening with correct bilinear data format (yield_force, plastic_motion) pairs

ROOT CAUSE FIX 1: For stories 2-4 (b=0, perfect plasticity), defined constant yield force hardening data (fy, 0.0) (fy, 1.0) since ABAQUS requires *CONNECTOR HARDENING when *CONNECTOR PLASTICITY is present

ROOT CAUSE FIX 2: *GLOBAL DAMPING has NO effect on CONN3D2 element models in ABAQUS (confirmed via damped vs undamped identical results). Replaced with explicit DASHPOT1 elements (mass-proportional, alpha*m_i to ground) and *CONNECTOR DAMPING (stiffness-proportional, beta*k_i in each connector). Same approach as the OpenSeesPy fix.
Added A, V to NODE OUTPUT for direct acceleration extraction (eliminates central-difference amplification of numerical noise)

matlab_vs_openseespy.reason: All peak response quantities match to within 0.002%. MATLAB and OpenSeesPy are in auditable agreement.

matlab_vs_abaqus.reason: All errors well under 10% threshold. Time-history correlations > 0.9994. ABAQUS now agrees with MATLAB to within 1.25% on all peak response quantities.

openseespy_vs_abaqus.reason: All errors well under 10% threshold. Three-software auditable agreement achieved.

thresholds.rationale: For nonlinear hysteretic response, peak acceleration and force tolerances may be looser than in linear cases, but displacement and base-shear errors above 10% indicate materially different nonlinear behavior and cannot be considered three-software agreement.

conclusion: MATLAB, OpenSeesPy, and ABAQUS independently produce auditable, numerically consistent nonlinear response results for Example 5. After correcting the OpenSeesPy output time convention, MATLAB and OpenSeesPy agree to about 0.0018% peak acceleration error and below 0.014% curve NRMSE. The remaining largest curve difference is MATLAB vs ABAQUS base shear NRMSE of about 2.013%, with correlation about 0.99946; peak response errors remain below 1.25%.

diagnostic_findings.root_cause_openseespy: ops.rayleigh(alpha, 0, beta, 0) stiffness-proportional damping non-functional in ops312. Fixed with explicit Viscous dampers C_i = beta * k0_i in parallel with each spring.
diagnostic_findings.root_cause_abaqus_1: *GLOBAL DAMPING has no effect on CONN3D2 element models (damped vs undamped produce identical results). Fixed with explicit DASHPOT1 elements (mass-proportional) and *CONNECTOR DAMPING (stiffness-proportional).
diagnostic_findings.root_cause_abaqus_2: *CONNECTOR HARDENING, TYPE=KINEMATIC requires non-zero yield force. For perfect plasticity (b=0), must use constant yield force data (fy,0.0)(fy,1.0) rather than omitting hardening.
diagnostic_findings.root_cause_abaqus_3: Original INP used HHT integration (ALPHA=-0.05, different Newmark parameters) and ISOTROPIC hardening. Changed to ALPHA=0 (pure Newmark) and KINEMATIC hardening.
diagnostic_findings.yield_pattern: Only story 1 (isolation layer, b=0.05) yields. Stories 2-4 (b=0) remain elastic throughout.
diagnostic_findings.damping_fix_shared: Both OpenSeesPy and ABAQUS required explicit damping element implementations to replace non-functional built-in Rayleigh damping.

implementation_audit.openseespy_time_axis_fix: OpenSeesPy recorder outputs start after the first transient step. The final output script now writes arrays directly from node/element responses, including an explicit initial t=0 state. This fixed a one-step time-label mismatch that inflated MATLAB/OpenSeesPy curve NRMSE while leaving peak values almost unchanged.
